- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.5) — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — add 3–7% to forecast to compensate.
- Avoid overreacting to recent spikes — smooth out forecast peaks by 1–2 days after sharp increases.
- Mean-revert forecasts toward 30-day moving average if sentiment is neutral or weak (sentiment 0.2–0.4).
- Lagged forecasts tend to be too low — adjust by +2–5% for the first 5–7 days of the forecast horizon.
- If sentiment is volatile or erratic, reduce forecast volatility — cap standard deviation at 2–3% of mean.
- Don’t assume momentum — if sentiment shifts sharply, reset forecast to recent 7-day average before adjusting.
